title: Code-world edit: a passing car merges into the ego lane
subtitle: Lyft Level 5, daytime urban arterial · model window 185 frames at 12 Hz (15.3 s) · single agent session (Claude Opus 5.5)
task: Edit the scenario in code: the car overtaking the ego on the left merges right into the ego lane ahead of the ego.

steps.label: Plan
steps.text:
One vehicle of a real scene is to change its behaviour in the most plausible way that remains clearly visible in the front camera. Among the permitted edit types (a lane change to the right, a parked car pulling out, a detour onto a side road), the choice depends on the scene: the ego trajectory cannot be edited, so any new manoeuvre must leave a safe gap to the ego as it actually drove.
Procedure: screen the 16 candidate scenes, shortlist by traffic and image quality, write the edit in `scene_world.py`, verify it with `sanity.py` (gaps to all agents and the ego, drivable area, divider crossings, visibility), revise until clean, then render the original and edited conditions and the BEV with `make_case.py`.
kv: 16 Lyft Level 5 scenes, 126 keyframes at 5 Hz each
keyframe 0 unchanged; static world and ego path fixed; model sees keyframes 0-76
no overlap or near-collision, on drivable road, correct-direction lanes, visible within ~40 m

# 3. read 6 real frames of each shortlisted scene

steps.label: Shortlist
steps.text: Scene A is ruled out because its truck already moves right in the recorded data. Scene B is overcast with a wet road. The ego in scene C travels at 13 m/s in the right-most travel lane, with parked cars along the curb, so a parked car pulling out or a car slowing for a right turn ahead of it would force the unchanged ego into a collision. A car that is already overtaking on the left and merges back ahead of the ego remains consistent with the recorded ego motion. Selected: scene C, vehicle 23852143.

steps.label: Edit v1: lane change to the right
steps.code:
# SAW: 23852143 overtakes the ego in the left lane: 3.7 m
#      to the left, 10-21 m ahead over keyframes 24-42,
#      ~16 m/s against 13 m/s for the ego

# 1. merge 3.5 m to the right over 4 s, once it is
#    about 11 m ahead of the ego
car = scene.agent('23852143d9391f3d...')
car.lane_change(-3.5, t0=28, t1=48)

# 2. gaps, road and visibility on the 12 Hz world
sanity.py --scene host-a009-... \
          --edited scene_world_v1.py

steps.label: Check: overlap after the model window
steps.text: The merge itself is clean (no overlap, on road, one lane-divider crossing, no road-divider crossing), but from 12 Hz frame 222 (keyframe ~92) the edited car overlaps 8b11c0. The car keeps its recorded overtaking speed in the new lane and runs into the slower car ahead of it. The collision lies after the model window, but it would appear in the canvas and the BEV.
kv: overlaps another agent in 77 frames (worst 8b11c0b38e @ 242, 0.94 of the smaller footprint)

steps.label: Edit v2: car following after the merge
steps.code:
# SAW: overlap with 8b11c0 from frame 222: in the new
#      lane the car keeps its overtaking speed (18 m/s),
#      while 8b11c0, which merges into the same lane at
#      keyframes 42-66, slows to 12-15 m/s

# 1. keep the lane change
car.lane_change(-3.5, t0=28, t1=48)

# 2. from keyframe 50, follow the speed of the car ahead
lead = scene.agent('8b11c0b38eb6456a...')
for t in range(50, 125):
    car.set_speed(lead.speed(t), from_t=t, to_t=t + 1)
#    -> centre distance to 8b11c0 stays at 22 m

# 3. re-check
sanity.py --scene host-a009-... \
          --edited scene_world_v2.py

steps.label: Check: clean
steps.text: No overlap anywhere in the clip. The smallest gap (1.27 m) is the lateral clearance to cars parked at the curb. The ego passes the same parked cars at 1.1-1.6 m. When the car crosses the lane line, the footprint gap to the ego is 15.5 m (about 1.2 s at 13 m/s), and the gap then grows. The edited speed profile is smoother than the recorded one.

# 2. compare original and edited canvas frame by frame

#    -> largest change at frame 92 (18,929 px)

steps.label: Canvas and BEV
steps.text: Frame 0 is bit-identical to the original. From frame 70 onward, the edited car moves from the left lane to directly in front of the ego and stays there (footprint gap to the ego 9-39 m within the model window). In the BEV, the dashed grey outline marks its original position in the left lane. A merge 4 keyframes earlier (keyframes 24-44) was also tested with `sanity.py`. It shortens the crossing gap from 15.5 m to 13 m without a noticeable gain in image size, so keyframes 28-48 were kept.
